rationale: CR-001, CR-002, and CR-005 are resolved with strong fix-up evidence, each confirmed end-to-end against a live PostgreSQL instance (not just unit tests). CR-002 (nested 'bedrock/converse/...' routing prefix) was re-assessed against real-world LiteLLM ecosystem conventions and found to be a documented real pattern, even though not yet observed in this exact telemetry source, so it was fixed defensively. CR-003 (multi-segment region prefix) and CR-004 (extended version-suffix shape) remain unresolved in code, but on explicit review the user accepted them as non-blocking: both were independently re-researched and found to have no basis in AWS's documented Bedrock naming conventions (always a single dot-segment region token; the version suffix baked into the base model ID, not an extensible appended tag), and the user, informed that 'fixing' them would mean loosening a match boundary with a real risk of introducing silent cross-model data collisions (strictly worse than today's visible under-normalization), explicitly chose to leave them as-is rather than code against unconfirmed, contradicted speculation. CR-006 (commit-format) similarly remains unresolved in code with explicit user acceptance: fixing it would require a destructive force-push rewriting an already-pushed commit on this open MR, and the repo's squash-merge-at-merge-time convention already gives the final merge commit the correct prefix regardless. All three open items are therefore accepted, recorded risk, not oversight, so the round is approved. No new high-risk issue was introduced by this round's fix-up (the only production change beyond CR-001 is one additive, narrowly-scoped '(bedrock/)?' wrapper, confirmed correct and non-regressive against all documented real variants on a live database).

finding_status.notes: Added the 'i' flag to the routing-prefix and provider-prefix regexp_replace calls (reader.py lines ~208-209). Reproduced the original bug and confirmed the fix end-to-end against a live PostgreSQL 17 instance (pgvector/pgvector:pg17, postgres-test container, port 5433): seeded cost_daily/session_dims with the 5 documented real raw-name variants (converse/{us,global,eu,jp}.anthropic...-v1:0 and the bare name) plus an uppercase probe (CONVERSE/US.ANTHROPIC...), ran the actual get_model_breakdown query through PostgresCliAnalyticsReader/asyncpg (not a mock). Before the fix: the uppercase variant stayed as its own row ('CONVERSE/US.ANTHROPIC.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001'). After the fix: all 6 rows merged into one 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001' row with session_count=6 and cost_usd=6.0 (correct sum), while claude-sonnet-5 and claude-sonnet-5-5 stayed distinct. Added test_normalization_is_case_insensitive (Python mirror) and updated the two SQL-shape pinned tests for the new flags; both run green. Verification script retained at docs/superpowers/reviews/2026-10-20-mr-4489/verify_model_breakdown.py.

Fixed: _normalized_model_name now strips an optional leading 'bedrock/' wrapper before the 'converse|invoke' routing token ('^(bedrock/)?(converse|invoke)/', case-insensitive). Basis: researched LiteLLM's documented Bedrock provider conventions, which nest an API-path marker behind the 'bedrock/' provider prefix (e.g. 'bedrock/converse/...') — a real pattern in that ecosystem, applied defensively even though not yet observed in this exact telemetry field. Verified end-to-end on the live PostgreSQL instance: seeded 'bedrock/converse/us.anthropic.claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0' alongside the 5 documented real variants and the CR-001 uppercase probe (7 rows total); all merged into one 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001' row with session_count=7, cost_usd=7.0 (correct sum), while claude-sonnet-5/claude-sonnet-5-5 stayed separate. Added test_normalization_strips_a_nested_bedrock_provider_wrapper (also confirms bare 'converse/'/'invoke/' still work unchanged) and updated the pinned-SQL tests; both run green.

Not fixed; explicitly accepted by the user as non-blocking after review. Reproduced on the live PostgreSQL instance: a compound two-segment prefix ('aws.us-east-1.anthropic...-v1:0') is left with 'aws.us-east-1.anthropic.' unstripped (only a single dot-segment, e.g. the already-supported GovCloud-style 'us-gov-west-1.anthropic.', is handled). Independently re-researched: AWS's documented Bedrock cross-region inference-profile ID format is always exactly one dot-segment ('<geo-prefix>.<provider>.<model-id>', the geo-prefix itself possibly hyphenated, e.g. 'us-gov-west-1') — no documented or observed real-world case of two separate dot-segments before the provider name. Fixing it would mean loosening the match boundary (e.g. repeating the optional group), which risks stripping part of a genuinely different model's own name and silently merging two distinct models' cost/session data — a worse failure mode (invisible data corruption) than today's visible under-normalization (an extra row). User reviewed this tradeoff and chose to accept the gap rather than fix speculatively; revisit only if real data surfaces this shape.

Not fixed; explicitly accepted by the user as non-blocking after review. Reproduced on the live PostgreSQL instance: 'claude-haiku-4-5-20251001-v1:0:1' (extra trailing segment after the version tag) is left completely unstripped. Independently re-researched: AWS's Bedrock model-ID version suffix is documented as exactly '-v<major>:<minor>', baked into the base model ID itself rather than a separately appended, extensible profile tag — no documented real-world shape with a further segment after the ':digits'. Same risk/tradeoff as CR-003 (loosening the trailing anchor risks silently merging distinct models' data). User reviewed this tradeoff and chose to accept the gap rather than fix speculatively; revisit only if real data surfaces this shape.

Added test_aggregation_merges_session_count_and_cost_across_raw_name_variants, which simulates get_model_breakdown's grouping semantics (COUNT(DISTINCT session_id), sum(cost_usd)) over cost_daily-shaped rows with mixed raw-name variants of the same canonical model, and asserts the merged counts/sums are correct while distinct models stay separate. Additionally verified the real aggregation end-to-end against the live PostgreSQL instance (same run as CR-001): 3 variants of claude-haiku-4-5-20251001 across 3 distinct sessions correctly summed to session_count=3 within the 6-row merged total. This closes the gap the finding identified (previously zero tests touched actual aggregation outcomes); it is a Python-level simulation rather than a committed live-DB pytest fixture, since no such fixture infrastructure exists yet in this test module and introducing one is beyond this fix's scope.
